findings.body: `website` is suppressed by `untrusted_attributes` for TL0 users seen anonymously, but the new `website_name` attribute is still serialized and rendered by `{{#if model.website_name}}` in user.hbs, so the spam-prone host and now also the full URL path of a TL0 user's site is exposed to anonymous visitors, defeating the existing restriction.
findings.failure_mode: Privacy/anti-spam restriction on TL0 profile websites is silently bypassed for anonymous requests.
findings.impact: `website` is suppressed by `untrusted_attributes` for TL0 users seen anonymously, but the new `website_name` attribute is still serialized and rendered by `{{#if model.website_name}}` in user.hbs, so the spam-prone host and now also the full URL path of a TL0 user's site is exposed to anonymous visitors, defeating the existing restriction.
findings.root_cause: A new derived attribute of the protected `website` field was registered in `attributes` without being registered in `untrusted_attributes`, so it inherits none of the field's visibility restrictions.
findings.suggested_fix: Add `:website_name` to the `untrusted_attributes` list (next to `:website`) so `include_website_name?` also returns false when `scope.restrict_user_fields?(object)` is true, and extend the `untrusted_attributes` spec array to include `website_name`.
findings.title: website_name bypasses untrusted_attributes and leaks TL0 users' website to anonymous
findings.trigger: An anonymous visitor requests /u/<username>.json for a trust-level-0 user who has filled in their profile website (the exact case exercised by the existing spec at spec/serializers/user_serializer_spec.rb:11-15).
findings.verifier_reason: Patch adds `:website_name` to `attributes` (line 43) but NOT to `untrusted_attributes` (lines 105-111 show only `:website` listed). The `untrusted_attributes` mechanism generates `include_<attr>?` methods that return false when `scope.restrict_user_fields?(object)` is true. Since `website_name` is not in that list, it bypasses the TL0 anonymous restriction. The spec at line 11 confirms `website` is in untrusted_attributes but `website_name` is absent.

findings.body: ActiveModel::Serializers only consults `include_<attr>?`, so this method is never called; `website_name` is unconditionally emitted (as `null`) instead of being omitted, contradicting the intended conditional inclusion and the surrounding convention (`include_card_image_badge_id?`, `include_email?`).
findings.failure_mode: Dead code: the guard never runs and the payload always contains the attribute.
findings.impact: ActiveModel::Serializers only consults `include_<attr>?`, so this method is never called; `website_name` is unconditionally emitted (as `null`) instead of being omitted, contradicting the intended conditional inclusion and the surrounding convention (`include_card_image_badge_id?`, `include_email?`).
findings.root_cause: The conditional-include hook was defined with the wrong method name (missing the trailing question mark required by the serializer framework).
findings.suggested_fix: Rename the method to `include_website_name?` so the conditional-inclusion hook is actually invoked.
findings.title: include_website_name lacks the `?` suffix so the attribute is always serialized
findings.trigger: Serializing any user whose profile website is blank (e.g. GET /u/<username>.json for a user that never set a website).
findings.verifier_reason: Patch line R153 shows `def include_website_name` without trailing `?`. ActiveModel::Serializers convention requires `include_<attr>?` for conditional inclusion (see `include_card_image_badge_id?` at line 161). Without the `?`, the method is never called by the serializer framework, making it dead code and causing unconditional serialization.

raw_findings.body: The anchor's `href` shows the newly saved URL while the visible link text still shows the old host/path, and if the website was previously empty the globe icon and link do not appear at all until a page reload.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Rendered link text and href disagree until the page is reloaded.
raw_findings.impact: The anchor's `href` shows the newly saved URL while the visible link text still shows the old host/path, and if the website was previously empty the globe icon and link do not appear at all until a page reload.
raw_findings.root_cause: The label was moved from a client-side computed property that tracked `model.website` to a server-computed attribute that is never refreshed after saving preferences.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Set `website_name` from the update response in `User#save` (alongside `bio_excerpt`), or keep a client-side computed fallback that derives the label from `model.website` when `website_name` is stale/absent.
raw_findings.title: Profile website label goes stale after editing the website in preferences
raw_findings.trigger: A user changes their website on /u/<name>/preferences (which binds directly to `model.website`) and then navigates back to their profile page without a full page reload; `User#save` only copies `bio_excerpt` from the response, so `website_name` keeps its previously serialized value.

raw_findings.body: A regression in the label-stripping comparison (or in its `> 2` guard, which misbehaves for multi-part TLDs such as `example.co.uk`) would not be caught by the suite.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Untested conditional branch allows silent behavioral regressions.
raw_findings.impact: A regression in the label-stripping comparison (or in its `> 2` guard, which misbehaves for multi-part TLDs such as `example.co.uk`) would not be caught by the suite.
raw_findings.root_cause: New multi-branch host-comparison logic was added but the accompanying spec only covers the equal-host, unrelated-host and parent-domain branches.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Add an example inside this context that stubs `Discourse.current_hostname` as `'forum.example.com'` with `user.user_profile.website = 'http://www.example.com/user'` and asserts the expected `website_name`, plus a negative case such as `'forum.other.com'`.
raw_findings.title: Sibling-subdomain branch of website_name has no spec coverage
raw_findings.trigger: The `elsif (website_host.split('.').length == discourse_host.split('.').length) && discourse_host.split('.').length > 2` branch (user_serializer.rb:144-146, e.g. website `http://www.example.com/user` on instance `forum.example.com`) is executed only in production; none of the three new examples stub a hostname with more than two labels while the website host also has more than two labels.

raw_findings.body: The hostnames compare unequal, all three branches fall through to returning only `website_host`, and the feature's goal (showing the complete path when the website domain matches the instance domain) silently fails for such entries.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Feature silently degrades to host-only display for mixed-case URLs.
raw_findings.impact: The hostnames compare unequal, all three branches fall through to returning only `website_host`, and the feature's goal (showing the complete path when the website domain matches the instance domain) silently fails for such entries.
raw_findings.root_cause: Hostname equality/suffix checks were written on raw, non-normalized host strings.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Downcase both values before comparing, e.g. `website_host = URI(website.to_s).host&.downcase` and `discourse_host = Discourse.current_hostname.downcase`, and use the downcased values in the subdomain checks too.
raw_findings.title: Host comparison in website_name is case-sensitive
raw_findings.trigger: A user stores their website with mixed-case host, e.g. `http://Example.com/user`, on an instance whose `Discourse.current_hostname` is `example.com`; Ruby's URI parser preserves the host casing.
